title: Automation API & SDK for Optimize: idempotent apply, webhook events, and staged rollback primitives
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Optimize generates batching and KV-caching configuration recommendations to reduce per-token cost while respecting latency SLOs. We need a hardened public/internal API and SDK primitives so partner teams and automation agents can safely apply recommendations, receive lifecycle events, and reliably rollback without creating unsafe serving states.

Goal: Deliver an API surface plus SDK helpers that provide idempotent `apply` semantics, webhook event notifications for recommendation lifecycle, and staged rollback primitives (canary -> full rollback) with built-in audit logging and retries. The surface must be safe for both hosted and Dedicated/Private deployments and support tenant-scoped RBAC.

High-level design summary:
- REST endpoints under /v1/optimize/automation for create/apply/status/rollback of recommendation bundles.
- Idempotency via an `Idempotency-Key` header (per-customer, per-resource) with server-side TTL (48h) and deduplication metadata stored in audit table.
- Webhook event types: recommendation.created, recommendation.applied.canary, recommendation.applied.full, recommendation.rollback.initiated, recommendation.rollback.completed, recommendation.failed. Each event contains recommendation_id, revision, model_variant, target_route, canary_fraction, owner, trace_id.
- SDK: language-neutral patterns and first-class helpers in the JS/Go SDKs: Optimize.applyRecommendation(options), Optimize.getRecommendationStatus(id), Optimize.rollbackRecommendation(id, {force:false}), helpers to register webhook handlers with signature verification and automatic retry backoff.
- Apply semantics: an apply is staged by default — first deploy to canary fraction (configurable, default 5%) then automatically progress to full after health checks pass. Canary progression can be gated by custom evals/metrics.
- Rollback semantics: rollback is reversible and records diff manifests. A rollback API returns an estimated impact summary and an audit token. Forced rollback is allowed for P0 incidents.

Acceptance criteria (must pass before release):
- Public API defined in OpenAPI v3 and published to internal API gateway.
- JS and Go SDKs implement idempotent Apply + rollback helpers and webhook verifier.
- Canary deployment flow is configurable per-apply and performs automated health checks (latency, error-rate, cost delta).
- Audit entries created for every apply/rollback with user, idempotency-key, diff, and trace_id.
- E2E tests simulating flaky infra to validate safe rollback and retries.
- Integration tests for webhook delivery, signature verification, and retry semantics.
- Documentation and example playbooks for partner teams.

API sketch (summary):
- POST /v1/optimize/automation/recommendations  -> create recommendation (body: manifest + target routes + suggested params). Headers: Authorization, Idempotency-Key. Returns: recommendation_id, revision.
- POST /v1/optimize/automation/recommendations/{id}/apply -> trigger staged apply. Body: {canary_fraction:int, gated_metrics:[], auto_promote:true|false}. Returns job_id and initial status.
- GET /v1/optimize/automation/recommendations/{id}/status -> returns state machine status and timeline.
- POST /v1/optimize/automation/recommendations/{id}/rollback -> rollback request. Body: {to_revision:int | to_snapshot_id:string, force:false}.
- GET /v1/optimize/automation/audit/{recommendation_id} -> returns audit log entries for UI and compliance.

Idempotency semantics (detailed):
- Idempotency-Key scope: {customer_id}:{resource_type} (e.g., cust-123:recommendation-apply). Server records outcome for 48h. Duplicate requests with same key and same payload will return the original result. If payload changes under same key return 412 Precondition Failed.
- Side effects must be recorded in an audit row and stored KV manifest so rollback can reconstruct prior state.

Observability and metrics:
- New metrics: optimize.apply.attempts, optimize.apply.success, optimize.apply.rollback_count, optimize.webhook.deliveries, optimize.webhook.failures, optimize.canary.promotions.
- Trace propagation: support Trace-ID header and include in webhook payloads.
- Console: per-recommendation timeline with token-level cost delta estimate and latency impact graph.

Security & compliance:
- Webhook signing with per-customer secret stored in KMS; SDKs should verify signatures.
- RBAC scopes: optimize:read, optimize:apply, optimize:rollback. Private deployments must honor local KMS and audit retention policy.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for idempotency store and TTL eviction.
- Integration tests with mock webhook endpoints to validate backoff and retry.
- Chaos tests to simulate partial apply (50% of canary nodes fail) and assert rollback occurs and audit captured.
- Fuzz tests for malformed idempotency headers and replay attempts.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flagged rollout (optimize_automation_api) starts internal-only -> staged enabling to top 5 customers -> open for self-serve.
- Canary percentage default 5% with opt-in to auto-promote.
- Monitor key metrics for 72h after enablement before wider rollouts.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Older clients without Idempotency-Key still allowed but receive warnings and will be assigned server-generated idempotency token with limited guarantees.
- Migration doc: teams must provide a migration window to add Idempotency-Key to their automation agents.

- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/Optimize+Automation+API+Design (internal)
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4729 (WIP)
- SDK proposal: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-proposals/pull/34

JS + Go SDKs ship helpers and webhook verifier with unit tests
Canary flow implemented with automated health checks and auto-promote toggle
Audit log entries created for every state transition and available via audit endpoint
E2E tests for rollback and idempotency pass in CI
Docs and playbooks published in the developer portal
design_notes: Store idempotency records in a write-optimized audit table with TTL; replicate to read replica for UI queries
Use event-sourced manifests: store diffs for apply so rollback composes original state deterministically
Canary promotion based on composite health score: latency P99, 5xx rate, and cost delta thresholds
Webhook delivery uses signed payloads with HMAC-SHA256 and per-customer secrets rotated quarterly
